title: Presenting the project and where it stands
grammar: Present Perfect × Past Simple (o que já foi feito × quando aconteceu)
objective: Nesta aula você vai separar de vez o Present Perfect do Past Simple. O Present Perfect (we have completed) mostra o resultado agora, sem dizer quando — é a língua do status report. O Past Simple (we completed last week) prende o fato a um momento passado. Como Project & Contract Manager, você usa os dois na mesma frase: 'We have finished the basic design; we approved it in March.'
intro: Every project update answers two different questions. What have we achieved so far? And when exactly did it happen? English uses two different tenses for those two questions, and mixing them up is the fastest way to confuse a client.

Use the Present Perfect for results that matter now: we have completed the basic design, we have not received the vendor drawings yet. Use the Past Simple as soon as you give a date: we completed it in March, the client approved it last Friday.
vocab: We have reached the second milestone of the contract.
The client approved the first deliverable in March.
We have already defined the scope of supply with the client.
The hand-over took place two weeks after the performance test.
I have just sent the monthly progress report.
We met the main stakeholders during the kick-off meeting.
practice: We have reached the second ______ of the contract.
milestone
The client approved the first ______ in March.
deliverable
We have already defined the ______ with the client.
scope of supply
The ______ took place two weeks after the performance test.
hand-over
I have just sent the monthly ______ to the steering committee.
progress report
We met every ______ during the kick-off meeting.
stakeholder
Each ______ has its own acceptance criteria.
deliverable
The ______ does not include the civil works.
scope of supply

audio.title: A two-minute project update
audio.text: Good morning. Let me give you a short update on the water treatment project. We have completed the basic engineering and we have released seventy per cent of the detailed drawings. We signed the contract in January and we held the kick-off meeting in the first week of February. Since then, the team has issued four progress reports. We have not received the pumps from the supplier yet, so the equipment milestone has moved. Last week I visited the site and I confirmed the civil schedule with the client. Overall, the project has stayed within budget.

readAloud: We have completed the basic engineering.
We signed the contract in January.
The client has already approved two deliverables.
I sent the progress report last Friday.
We have not received the vendor drawings yet.
fill: We ___ the basic engineering, so we can start detailing. (complete)
The client ___ the first deliverable last March. (approve)
I ___ four progress reports so far this year. (issue)
We ___ the vendor drawings yet. (not receive)
The team ___ the kick-off meeting two weeks ago. (hold)
The project ___ within budget since the beginning. (stay)
I ___ the site last week and everything was in order. (visit)
qa: What have you completed so far?
We have completed the basic engineering and most of the drawings.
When did you sign the contract?
We signed it in January.
Have you received the vendor drawings?
No, we have not received them yet.
How many progress reports have you issued?
We have issued four progress reports so far.
When did the client approve the first deliverable?
The client approved it last March.
sentences: We have completed the basic engineering.
We signed the contract in January.
The client has already approved two deliverables.
We have not received the vendor drawings yet.
I sent the progress report last Friday.
The project has stayed within budget so far.
We held the kick-off meeting two weeks ago.
We have reached the second milestone of the contract.
grammarPoint:
Present Perfect = have/has + particípio. Fala do resultado agora, sem dizer quando: We have completed the design. — Concluímos o projeto básico (e ele está pronto agora).

Past Simple = verbo no passado. Fala de um momento passado fechado: We completed the design in March. — Concluímos em março.

A regra prática: apareceu uma data (in March, last week, yesterday, in 2025, two weeks ago) → Past Simple. Não apareceu data, e o que importa é o placar de hoje → Present Perfect.
deepDive:
Palavras que puxam o Present Perfect: already (já), yet (ainda — em negativas e perguntas), just (acabou de), so far (até agora), since (desde), for (há/por), never, ever.

Palavras que puxam o Past Simple: yesterday, last week/month, ago, in January, when.

O par que aparece em todo status report: primeiro o resultado, depois a data. We have finished the P&ID package. We issued it on 12 May.

Atenção: since marca o começo (since January) e for marca a duração (for six months). Os dois pedem Present Perfect: We have worked on this scope since January / for six months.
examples: We have completed the basic engineering.
Concluímos o projeto básico.
We completed the basic engineering in March.
Concluímos o projeto básico em março.
The client has already approved the deliverable.
O cliente já aprovou o entregável.
The client approved the deliverable last Friday.
O cliente aprovou o entregável na sexta passada.
We have not received the pumps yet.
Ainda não recebemos as bombas.
We have worked on this contract since January.
Trabalhamos neste contrato desde janeiro.
I have just sent the progress report.
Acabei de enviar o relatório de andamento.
I sent the progress report two hours ago.
Enviei o relatório há duas horas.
mistakes: We have completed it last March.
We completed it last March.
Com data fechada (last March) use o Past Simple.
I already sent the report.
I have already sent the report.
Com already, sem data, o natural é o Present Perfect.
We have sign the contract.
We have signed the contract.
Depois de have vem o particípio (signed), não o infinitivo.
We didn't received the drawings.
We didn't receive the drawings.
Depois de didn't o verbo volta à forma base.
We work on this project since January.
We have worked on this project since January.
Com since a estrutura é have/has + particípio.

celebrate.en: Well done. You can now open any project update with the two tenses a client expects: what has been achieved, and exactly when it happened.
celebrate.pt: Muito bem. Agora você abre qualquer atualização de projeto com os dois tempos que o cliente espera: o que já foi conquistado e quando exatamente aconteceu.

title: Scope, WBS and deliverables
grammar: Voz passiva (present e past) — the scope is defined / was approved
objective: Nesta aula você vai dominar a voz passiva, a estrutura mais usada em documento de projeto e contrato. Em inglês técnico o foco é o que foi feito, não quem fez: 'The scope is divided into four packages', 'The drawings were approved by the client'. Você vai aprender a montar a passiva no presente e no passado e a usar 'by' só quando o autor realmente importa.
intro: Open any contract, any WBS, any technical specification, and you will find the same structure again and again: the scope is divided, the work is split into packages, the drawings were approved, the exclusions were listed in Annex II.

This is the passive voice, and it is not a style choice. In project documents the important information is the deliverable itself, not the person who produced it. Today you build the passive with be + past participle, in the present and in the past.
vocab: The project is organised in a work breakdown structure with four levels.
The scope is divided into five packages.
The acceptance criteria were agreed during the kick-off meeting.
All exclusions are listed in Annex II of the contract.
The interface between civil and mechanical is defined in this drawing.
Everything outside the battery limit is excluded from our supply.
practice: The project is organised in a ______ with four levels.
work breakdown structure
The scope is divided into five ______.
package
The ______ were agreed during the kick-off meeting.
acceptance criteria
Every ______ is listed in Annex II of the contract.
exclusion
The ______ between civil and mechanical is defined in this drawing.
interface
Everything outside the ______ is excluded from our supply.
battery limit
Each ______ has its own budget and its own schedule.
package
The ______ must be signed before the performance test.
acceptance criteria

audio.title: How the scope is organised
audio.text: Let me explain how the scope is organised. The project is divided into five packages: civil, mechanical, electrical, piping and instrumentation. Each package is broken down into deliverables, and every deliverable is assigned to a discipline leader. The work breakdown structure was prepared during the basic engineering phase and it was approved by the client in March. The battery limits are shown on drawing zero zero one. Anything outside those limits is not included in our supply. The exclusions were listed in Annex two and they were discussed line by line with the client.

readAloud: The scope is divided into five packages.
The drawings were approved by the client in March.
Every deliverable is assigned to a discipline leader.
The exclusions were listed in Annex II.
The battery limits are shown on drawing 001.
fill: The drawings ___ by the client last March. (approve)
Every deliverable ___ to a discipline leader. (assign)
The WBS ___ during the basic engineering phase. (prepare)
This scope ___ in the original contract. (not include)
The interfaces ___ line by line with the client. (discuss)
qa: How is the scope organised?
The scope is divided into five packages.
When were the drawings approved?
They were approved by the client in March.
Where are the exclusions listed?
They are listed in Annex II of the contract.
Is the civil work included in your supply?
No, it is not included. It is outside the battery limit.
Who prepared the work breakdown structure?
It was prepared by our engineering team during basic design.
sentences: The scope is divided into five packages.
The drawings were approved by the client in March.
Every deliverable is assigned to a discipline leader.
The exclusions are listed in Annex II.
This item is not included in our scope of supply.
The work breakdown structure was prepared during basic engineering.
The battery limits are shown on drawing 001.
The acceptance criteria were agreed at the kick-off meeting.
grammarPoint:
Voz passiva = be + particípio passado.

Presente: is / are + particípio — The scope is divided into five packages.
Passado: was / were + particípio — The drawings were approved in March.
Negativa: This item is not included in our scope.
Modal: The report must be signed before the test.

Use by só quando o autor importa: approved by the client. Se não importa, deixe de fora — é o padrão de documento técnico.
deepDive:
Por que a passiva domina o documento de projeto: ela coloca o entregável no início da frase, que é o que o leitor procura. Compare: We divided the scope into five packages (foco em nós) × The scope is divided into five packages (foco no escopo).

Cuidado com o particípio irregular: write → written, send → sent, take → taken, give → given, make → made, show → shown, hold → held, build → built.

Passiva com modal — muito útil em contrato: can be supplied, must be approved, should be confirmed, will be delivered, cannot be changed without a variation order.

Verbos que quase sempre aparecem na passiva em engenharia: divide, include, exclude, assign, list, show, define, agree, approve, issue, install, commission.
examples: The scope is divided into five packages.
O escopo é dividido em cinco pacotes.
The drawings were approved by the client.
Os desenhos foram aprovados pelo cliente.
This item is not included in our supply.
Este item não está incluído no nosso fornecimento.
The exclusions were listed in Annex II.
As exclusões foram listadas no Anexo II.
The report must be signed before the test.
O relatório precisa ser assinado antes do teste.
The equipment will be delivered in September.
O equipamento será entregue em setembro.
The interfaces are defined on drawing 001.
As interfaces são definidas no desenho 001.
The WBS was prepared during basic engineering.
A EAP foi elaborada durante o projeto básico.
mistakes: The scope is divide into five packages.
The scope is divided into five packages.
Depois de be entra o particípio: divided, não divide.
The drawings was approved in March.
The drawings were approved in March.
Sujeito plural (drawings) pede were.
This item is not include in our scope.
This item is not included in our scope.
Na negativa o particípio continua: is not included.
The report must be sign by the client.
The report must be signed by the client.
Depois de modal + be vem o particípio: signed.
The exclusions were listed for the client.
The exclusions were listed by the client.
O autor da ação vem com by, não com for.
quick: This item ___ in our supply. (not include)
The report ___ before the test. (must / sign)

celebrate.en: Excellent. The passive voice is the grammar of contracts and specifications — and you can now read it, write it and defend it in a scope discussion.
celebrate.pt: Excelente. A voz passiva é a gramática dos contratos e das especificações — e agora você lê, escreve e defende escopo com ela.

title: Schedule, milestones and the critical path
grammar: Formas de futuro — will / going to / present continuous para agenda
objective: Nesta aula você vai escolher a forma de futuro certa para cada situação de cronograma. 'Will' para decisões e promessas no momento da fala ('I'll send it today'), 'going to' para o plano já decidido ('We're going to mobilise in May') e o present continuous para compromisso agendado ('The FAT is taking place on 14 June'). Errar isso soa amador em reunião de cronograma.
intro: Three ways of talking about the future, three different messages. A client hears the difference immediately, even if they never studied the rule.

I will send you the revised schedule — a decision I make right now. We are going to mobilise the site team in May — a plan already made. The factory acceptance test is taking place on 14 June — a fixed appointment in the diary. Today you learn to pick the right one.
vocab: Any delay on the critical path is going to push the whole project.
This activity has three weeks of float, so we will not lose the milestone.
The lead time for the fan is going to be twenty weeks.
Mobilisation is taking place in the first week of May.
I will send the three-week look-ahead every Monday.
We are going to revise the baseline after the change order.
practice: Any delay on the ______ is going to push the whole project.
critical path
This activity has three weeks of ______, so we will not lose the milestone.
float
The ______ for the fan is going to be twenty weeks.
lead time
______ is taking place in the first week of May.
Mobilisation
I will send the three-week ______ every Monday.
look-ahead
We are going to revise the ______ after the change order.
baseline
The pumps are on the ______, so we cannot lose a single day.
critical path
A long ______ from the supplier changes the whole sequence.
lead time

audio.title: The schedule for the next quarter
audio.text: Here is the plan for the next quarter. We are going to freeze the detailed engineering at the end of April. Mobilisation is taking place in the first week of May, and the civil contractor is starting on site on the eighth. The fan has a twenty week lead time, so it sits on the critical path. If the purchase order slips, the erection date is going to move as well. I will send you a three week look ahead every Monday morning, and I will flag any activity with less than five days of float. We are not going to change the baseline unless the client issues a variation order.

readAloud: I will send you the revised schedule today.
We are going to mobilise the site team in May.
The factory acceptance test is taking place on 14 June.
This activity is on the critical path.
We are not going to change the baseline this month.
fill: I ___ you the look-ahead every Monday. (send)
We ___ the site team in May. It is already agreed. (going to / mobilise)
The FAT ___ on 14 June. It is in the diary. (take place)
If the pump slips, the erection date ___ as well. (going to / move)
Don't worry — I ___ the client this afternoon. (call)
We ___ the baseline unless the client issues a change order. (not going to / revise)
The civil contractor ___ on site on the eighth. (start)
I promise I ___ you as soon as I have the date. (inform)
qa: When are you going to mobilise the site team?
We are going to mobilise in the first week of May.
When is the factory acceptance test taking place?
It is taking place on 14 June.
Can you send me the look-ahead?
Yes, I will send it to you this afternoon.
What happens if the fan is late?
If the fan is late, the erection date is going to move.
Are you going to change the baseline?
No, we are not going to change it without a variation order.
sentences: I will send you the revised schedule today.
We are going to mobilise the site team in May.
The factory acceptance test is taking place on 14 June.
This activity is on the critical path.
The lead time for the fan is twenty weeks.
We are not going to change the baseline without a variation order.
I will flag any activity with less than five days of float.
The civil contractor is starting on site on the eighth.
grammarPoint:
will → decisão tomada agora, promessa, oferta: I'll send it this afternoon.

be going to → plano ou intenção já decidida, e previsão com evidência: We're going to mobilise in May. / The date is going to move.

Present continuous (am/is/are + -ing) → compromisso agendado, com data e hora: The FAT is taking place on 14 June.

Na prática: agenda → present continuous; plano → going to; promessa na hora → will.
deepDive:
O teste rápido: a data já está no calendário e combinada com outra parte? Use o present continuous. É só uma intenção da sua equipe? Use going to. Você acabou de decidir enquanto fala? Use will.

Previsão com prova × previsão com opinião: Look at the curve — we're going to miss the milestone (há evidência) × I think we'll recover in June (opinião). Depois de I think, I'm sure, probably, o normal é will.

Em cláusula de tempo e condição, futuro não usa will: I'll call you when the drawings arrive (não: when the drawings will arrive). If the pump slips, the date will move.

Contrações que soam naturais em call: I'll, we'll, it'll, we're going to (falado: "we're gonna" — entenda, mas escreva completo).
examples: I will send you the revised schedule today.
Vou te enviar o cronograma revisado hoje.
We are going to mobilise the site team in May.
Vamos mobilizar a equipe de campo em maio.
The FAT is taking place on 14 June.
O teste de fábrica acontece no dia 14 de junho.
The erection date is going to move.
A data de montagem vai mudar.
I'll call the supplier this afternoon.
Eu ligo para o fornecedor esta tarde.
We are not going to change the baseline.
Não vamos alterar a linha de base.
I'll confirm as soon as the drawings arrive.
Confirmo assim que os desenhos chegarem.
The civil contractor is starting on the eighth.
A empreiteira civil começa no dia oito.
mistakes: I will to send the schedule.
I will send the schedule.
Depois de will o verbo vem sem to.
We are going mobilise in May.
We are going to mobilise in May.
A estrutura é going to + verbo.
The FAT is take place on 14 June.
The FAT is taking place on 14 June.
No present continuous o verbo leva -ing.
I'll call you when the drawings will arrive.
I'll call you when the drawings arrive.
Depois de when o futuro vira presente.
We will mobilise in May, it is already agreed.
We are going to mobilise in May.
Plano já combinado pede going to, não will.
quick: I ___ the report this afternoon. (will / send)
We ___ the team in May. (going to / mobilise)
I'll call you when the pump ___ . (arrive)
The date ___ if the fan is late. (going to / move)

celebrate.en: Great work. You now have three futures instead of one — and a client can hear the difference between a promise, a plan and an appointment.
celebrate.pt: Ótimo trabalho. Agora você tem três futuros em vez de um — e o cliente ouve a diferença entre uma promessa, um plano e um compromisso marcado.

title: The water treatment package
grammar: Orações relativas — defining × non-defining (which / that / who / where)
objective: Nesta aula você vai juntar duas informações numa frase só com orações relativas — a estrutura que descreve equipamento sem repetir o substantivo. Você vai ver a diferença entre a defining ('the pump that feeds the clarifier'), que identifica qual é, e a non-defining ('the clarifier, which was supplied in 2023, ...'), que só acrescenta informação e vem entre vírgulas.
intro: A water treatment plant is a chain of equipment, and describing it means constantly saying which one you mean. The tank that receives the effluent. The pump which feeds the clarifier. The engineer who signed the datasheet.

That is a defining relative clause: it tells the listener which item you are talking about. A non-defining clause does something different — it adds extra information between commas, and you could delete it without losing the identification.
vocab: The tank that receives the effluent has a capacity of 300 cubic metres.
The clarifier, which was supplied in 2023, is still under warranty.
The pump which handles the sludge needs a special impeller.
The dosing skid that we designed is fully automatic.
This is the meter that measures the flow rate at the inlet.
The line where the make-up water enters is shown in red.
practice: The tank that receives the ______ has a capacity of 300 cubic metres.
effluent
The ______, which was supplied in 2023, is still under warranty.
clarifier
The pump which handles the ______ needs a special impeller.
sludge
The ______ skid that we designed is fully automatic.
dosing
This is the meter that measures the ______ at the inlet.
flow rate
The line where the ______ enters is shown in red.
make-up water
The chemical ______ is controlled by the PLC.
dosing
The operator who checks the ______ level works the night shift.
sludge

audio.title: A walk through the water treatment package
audio.text: Let me take you through the water treatment package. This is the equalisation tank, which receives the effluent from the process area. The pump that feeds the clarifier is on the left, and it is the only pump that has a stand by unit. The clarifier, which was supplied in twenty twenty three, is still under warranty. Behind it you can see the dosing skid that our team designed. The engineer who prepared the datasheets is Marcelo, and he is the person you should contact for any technical question. The line where the make up water enters is the one marked in red on the drawing.

readAloud: This is the pump that feeds the clarifier.
The clarifier, which was supplied in 2023, is still under warranty.
The engineer who signed the datasheet is Marcelo.
This is the line where the make-up water enters.
The only pump that has a stand-by unit is this one.
fill: This is the pump ___ feeds the clarifier. (that)
The clarifier, ___ was supplied in 2023, is under warranty. (which)
The engineer ___ signed the datasheet is Marcelo. (who)
This is the area ___ the sludge is dewatered. (where)
The tank ___ receives the effluent is 300 cubic metres. (that)
Marcelo, ___ prepared the datasheets, is on holiday. (who)
The dosing skid ___ we designed is fully automatic. (that)
The report, ___ we issued last week, covers the whole package. (which)
qa: Which pump feeds the clarifier?
The pump that is on the left feeds the clarifier.
Is the clarifier still under warranty?
Yes. The clarifier, which was supplied in 2023, is still under warranty.
Who signed the datasheets?
Marcelo, who is our process engineer, signed them.
Where does the make-up water enter?
It enters through the line that is marked in red.
What does the dosing skid do?
It is the skid that injects the chemicals automatically.
sentences: This is the pump that feeds the clarifier.
The clarifier, which was supplied in 2023, is still under warranty.
The engineer who signed the datasheet is Marcelo.
This is the line where the make-up water enters.
The tank that receives the effluent has a capacity of 300 cubic metres.
The dosing skid that we designed is fully automatic.
Marcelo, who prepared the datasheets, is the technical contact.
The only pump that has a stand-by unit is this one.
grammarPoint:
Defining (identifica qual é — sem vírgula): The pump that feeds the clarifier is on the left. Se tirar a oração, ninguém sabe de qual bomba você fala.

Non-defining (só acrescenta — entre vírgulas): The clarifier, which was supplied in 2023, is under warranty. Se tirar, a frase continua identificando o equipamento.

Os pronomes: who = pessoa · which = coisa · that = pessoa ou coisa (só em defining) · where = lugar · whose = posse.
deepDive:
Regra de ouro: that nunca entra em oração entre vírgulas. Non-defining é sempre which ou who.

Quando dá para omitir o pronome: quando ele é objeto da oração. The skid (that) we designed is automatic. — aqui we é o sujeito, então that pode sumir. Mas The pump that feeds the clarifier não perde o that, porque ele é o sujeito.

Non-defining sobre a frase inteira: The pump failed, which delayed the whole test. — o which se refere ao fato todo. Muito útil em relatório de ocorrência.

where × in which: the area where the sludge is dewatered = the area in which the sludge is dewatered (a segunda é mais formal, para especificação).
examples: This is the pump that feeds the clarifier.
Esta é a bomba que alimenta o decantador.
The clarifier, which was supplied in 2023, is under warranty.
O decantador, que foi fornecido em 2023, está na garantia.
The engineer who signed the datasheet is Marcelo.
O engenheiro que assinou a folha de dados é o Marcelo.
This is the area where the sludge is dewatered.
Esta é a área onde o lodo é desidratado.
The skid we designed is fully automatic.
O skid que projetamos é totalmente automático.
The pump failed, which delayed the whole test.
A bomba falhou, o que atrasou o teste inteiro.
We use the supplier whose lead time is shorter.
Usamos o fornecedor cujo prazo de entrega é menor.
The only pump that has a stand-by unit is this one.
A única bomba que tem unidade reserva é esta.
mistakes: The clarifier, that was supplied in 2023, is new.
The clarifier, which was supplied in 2023, is new.
Entre vírgulas nunca se usa that — use which.
The engineer which signed the datasheet is Marcelo.
The engineer who signed the datasheet is Marcelo.
Para pessoa use who.
This is the pump that it feeds the clarifier.
This is the pump that feeds the clarifier.
O pronome relativo já é o sujeito; não repita it.
The area where the sludge is dewatered there.
The area where the sludge is dewatered.
Com where não se repete o advérbio de lugar.
The report which we issued it last week.
The report which we issued last week.
Não repita o objeto depois do verbo.
quick: This is the pump ___ feeds the clarifier.
The clarifier, ___ was supplied in 2023, is new.
The engineer ___ signed the datasheet is Marcelo.
This is the area ___ the sludge is dewatered.
We chose the supplier ___ lead time is shorter.

celebrate.en: Very good. You can now describe a whole equipment package in one clear sentence — and a comma is all it takes to change the meaning.
celebrate.pt: Muito bom. Agora você descreve um pacote inteiro de equipamentos numa frase clara — e basta uma vírgula para mudar o sentido.

title: Dust control: reading the numbers
grammar: Modais de dedução — must be / can't be / might be / could be
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a falar sobre o que os números provavelmente significam, sem afirmar o que ainda não foi comprovado. 'The pressure drop is high, so a bag must be blinded' (quase certeza), 'it can't be the fan' (impossível), 'it might be a leak in the hopper' (possível). É a linguagem do troubleshooting técnico com o cliente — firme, mas honesta.
intro: A baghouse tells you what is happening through numbers: differential pressure, opacity, air-to-cloth ratio. Reading those numbers out loud in front of a client is a skill of its own, because you must sound confident without promising a diagnosis you have not confirmed.

English gives you a scale for that. Must be for near certainty. Can't be for impossibility. Might be, may be and could be for genuine possibility. Today you place your engineering judgement on that scale.
vocab: The differential pressure in the baghouse must be too high.
A differential pressure of 250 millimetres can't be normal.
If the opacity is rising, a bag might be torn.
The cleaning is weak, so the compressed air pressure could be low.
The hopper may be full, and that would explain the re-entrainment.
With this flow the air-to-cloth ratio must be above the design value.
practice: The differential pressure in the ______ must be too high.
baghouse
A ______ of 250 millimetres can't be normal.
differential pressure
If the ______ is rising, a bag might be torn.
opacity
The cleaning is weak, so the ______ pressure could be low.
compressed air
The ______ may be full, and that would explain the re-entrainment.
hopper
With this flow the ______ must be above the design value.
air-to-cloth ratio

audio.title: Looking at the trend before the meeting
audio.text: Look at this trend before we meet the client. The differential pressure went from one hundred to two hundred and forty millimetres in three weeks. That can't be normal wear, it is far too fast. The bags must be blinding, and the most likely cause is moisture. It could be a leak in the hopper, or the gas might be entering below the dew point during start up. It can't be the fan, because the flow has not changed at all. I would not promise a diagnosis today. I will say the evidence suggests moisture and that we may need an inspection before we confirm anything.

grammarPoint:
Modal + be = o quanto você tem de certeza agora.

must be → quase certeza, com evidência: The bags must be blinding.
can't be → impossível (o oposto de must be): That can't be normal wear.
might be / may be / could be → possível, sem confirmação: It might be a leak.

Nunca use mustn't para dedução — mustn't é proibição. O contrário de must be é can't be.
deepDive:
A escala completa, do mais forte ao mais fraco: must be (95%) → should be (esperado) → may be / might be / could be (50%) → can't be (0%).

Para deduzir sobre algo em andamento: modal + be + -ing. The bags must be blinding. / The gas might be entering below the dew point.

Para deduzir sobre o passado: modal + have + particípio. A bag must have failed during the night. / It can't have been the fan. / Moisture might have entered during start-up.

Cuidado com o par may be × maybe: It may be a leak (verbo) × Maybe it is a leak (advérbio, começa a frase). São coisas diferentes.

As mangas devem estar colmatando.
That can't be normal wear.
Isso não pode ser desgaste normal.
It might be a leak in the hopper.
Pode ser um vazamento na moega.

A pressão do ar comprimido pode estar baixa.

Uma manga deve ter falhado durante a noite.
It can't have been the fan.
Não pode ter sido o ventilador.

Pode ter entrado umidade durante a partida.

mistakes: That mustn't be normal wear.
That can't be normal wear.
Para dizer que é impossível use can't be; mustn't é proibição.
The bags must to be blinding.
The bags must be blinding.
Depois de modal não entra to.
It might is a leak.
It might be a leak.
Depois do modal vem be, na forma base.
A bag must failed during the night.
A bag must have failed during the night.
Dedução sobre o passado pede must have + particípio.
Maybe be a leak in the hopper.
It may be a leak in the hopper.
may be é verbo; maybe é advérbio e abre a frase.
